hookLine: Soda giants love a bold campaign. Let's rank the craziest ones from Pepsi and Coca-Cola.

items.voiceLine: Pepsi had Kendall Jenner end a protest by handing a cop a can of soda. It got pulled within 24 hours and is still the textbook example of a brand missing the point. D-Tier, an all-time misfire.

But the original 'Pepsi Challenge' had real people blind taste-testing on the street and picking Pepsi on camera. Simple, confident, and it actually worked for decades. B-Tier, advertising built on an actual dare.
Coca-Cola's Polar Bears ad turned a soda break into a whole animated world, no dialogue needed. Warm, charming, instantly recognizable. A-Tier, they made a mascot out of nothing.

But 'Holidays Are Coming' basically invented the modern idea of Christmas starting with a truck covered in lights. People still say the holidays haven't started until they see it. S-Tier, they own an entire season.
